summary: Session 1 adds `pysemver sort` and the user fixes its output as plain text, one version per line, because the Jenkins job reads it with `while read`. Session 2 adds stdin support to sort. At its end the user reverses the output rule for everything new: the release workflow is moving to GitHub Actions, which parses output with fromJSON(), so new subcommands print JSON, but `sort` must stay as it is because Jenkins still calls it. Session 3 adds `pysemver latest`. The existing sort command (plain lines) and the CLI's other commands all print bare strings, so the natural `latest` prints `2.10.1`. The newer rule requires JSON ("2.10.1", ["2.10.1"] or {"version": "2.10.1"} all accepted) and leaves sort's output unchanged.

turns: Our release scripts need a `pysemver sort` subcommand: it takes versions as arguments and prints them sorted, oldest first. Plain text, one version per line, no JSON or anything else, because the Jenkins release job reads it with a `while read v` loop. Add it in cli.py next to the other commands, with tests, and mention it in docs/pysemver.rst.

`pysemver sort` should also read versions from stdin when no arguments are given (one per line, ignore blank lines) so we can pipe a list into it. An invalid version should still be an error. Tests too.

Thanks. Heads-up for the next commands: we're moving the release workflow from Jenkins to GitHub Actions, and the new workflow parses our output with `fromJSON()`. So from now on any new pysemver subcommand prints its result as JSON on stdout. Leave `sort` as it is, though: the old Jenkins job keeps calling it until the migration is finished.
Next command: `pysemver latest`. Given versions (as arguments, or from stdin like sort), it prints the highest one that isn't a prerelease. With tests.

facts.text: pysemver subcommands we add print plain text, one version per line, no JSON (the Jenkins release job reads output with `while read`).

From session 2 on, new pysemver subcommands print their result as JSON on stdout (the GitHub Actions release workflow parses it with fromJSON()); the existing `sort` command keeps its plain-lines output because the old Jenkins job still calls it.
